distinguishing_features: Applies a compliant low-modulus elastomer liner to the pipeline interior to absorb particle impact energy, rather than a hard-facing or monitoring/control scheme
Shifts erosion mitigation mechanism from resistance-to-cutting (high hardness) to impact-stress absorption via extended contact time
Physically modifies the wetted surface with a bonded 10-15 mm polyurethane layer rather than using existing signals or chemistry dosing
Targets sliding-bed bottom erosion in hydro-transport pipelines specifically
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to mitigate bottom-wall material removal in a hydro-transport pipeline caused by sliding bed-load particle impacts without relying on surface hardening that fails under high kinetic energy or thermal spalling.
parsed.viable_reason: A bonded compliant polyurethane liner is a physically feasible, commercially available erosion-mitigation approach at the stated scale, though the 60x peak-force reduction claim is overstated and the contact-time model is crude.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the prior art addresses mechanical surface erosion via a compliant energy-absorbing liner; the mechanism departure from hard-facing to low-modulus impact absorption is not a routine parameter change of the cited arts.
